questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: When a cell population grows geometrically in a limited nutrient supply and its growth is plotted against time, a sigmoid curve is obtained. In which phase of this curve is the growth fastest?

solution.explanation: In geometric growth the initial growth is slow (lag phase), then it increases rapidly at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase), when both progeny cells of each division keep dividing. With limited nutrients, growth then slows down and levels off in the stationary phase.
steps: Log/exponential phase: rapid growth, both daughter cells keep dividing
Stationary phase: growth slows because nutrients become limiting
solution.why_others_wrong: The lag and stationary phases are the slow parts of the curve. The phase of maturation is a zone of the growing root or shoot, not a phase of the sigmoid curve.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth rates: geometric growth and the sigmoid curve
solution.final_answer: Option B: Log (exponential) phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Grape growers use a plant growth regulator to increase the length of grape stalks. The regulator used is:

solution.explanation: Gibberellins cause an increase in the length of the axis. This ability is used commercially to increase the length of grape stalks.
steps: Increase in length of axis → gibberellins
solution.why_others_wrong: ABA is a growth inhibitor; ethylene promotes ripening and abscission; cytokinins promote cell division and lateral shoot growth, not axis elongation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', gibberellins: physiological effects
solution.final_answer: Option D: Gibberellins

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Abscisic acid is also called the stress hormone because it increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses.
Statement II: Abscisic acid promotes seed germination.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Growth in plants can be measured as an increase in cell number. According to NCERT, a single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than:

A single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, whereas cells in a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times.
steps: Maize root apical meristem → over 17,500 new cells per hour
3,50,000 is the increase in size of watermelon cells, not a cell count
solution.why_others_wrong: 3,50,000 refers to the increase in cell size in watermelon. The other options change the number or the time unit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) is widely applied in tea plantations and in hedge-making.
Reason (R): In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds; removing the shoot tip usually results in the growth of the lateral buds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Auxin produced by the growing apical bud suppresses the lateral buds (apical dominance). Decapitation removes this inhibition, so lateral buds grow and the plant becomes bushy. That is exactly why decapitation is used in tea plantations (more leafy shoots) and hedge-making (dense growth).
steps: A: true, NCERT's applications of decapitation
R: true, definition of apical dominance and effect of decapitation
Lateral buds grow after decapitation → bushy plants → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', auxins: apical dominance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about auxins are correct?

(a) Auxins help to initiate rooting in stem cuttings.
(b) Auxins promote flowering, for example in pineapples.
(c) NAA and 2,4-D are natural auxins isolated from plants.
(d) Auxins control xylem differentiation and help in cell division.
(e) Auxins are produced mainly in mature leaves and roots and move to the growing apices.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Auxins are generally produced by the growing apices of stems and roots, from where they migrate to their regions of action. IAA and IBA are isolated from plants; NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D are synthetic auxins. Auxins initiate rooting in stem cuttings, promote flowering in pineapple, control xylem differentiation and help in cell division.
steps: (e) False: auxins are produced at the growing apices of stems and roots
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', auxins
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Differentiation in plants is closed, because cells derived from the same meristem always mature into the same kind of structure.
Statement II: Development in plants is under the control of intrinsic factors, such as genetic factors and plant growth regulators, as well as extrinsic factors such as light, temperature, water, oxygen and nutrition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Open differentiation and control of development
solution.explanation: Differentiation in plants is open: cells or tissues arising from the same meristem have different structures at maturity. Development is controlled by intrinsic factors (intracellular genetic factors and intercellular chemicals such as PGRs) and by extrinsic factors (light, temperature, water, oxygen, nutrition).
steps: Statement I: false, differentiation in plants is open
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; development
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A callus of mass 2 g grows geometrically according to W₁ = W₀e^(rt), with relative growth rate r = 0.231 per day. Taking ln 2 = 0.693, what will be its mass after 9 days?

solution.explanation: In geometric growth W₁ = W₀e^(rt). Here rt = 0.231 × 9 = 2.079 = 3 × 0.693 = 3 ln 2, so e^(rt) = 2³ = 8. W₁ = 2 g × 8 = 16 g.
solution.shortcut: rt is three times ln 2, so the callus doubles three times: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 g.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.2 g uses the arithmetic form W₀(1 + rt). 8 g is e^(rt) alone, forgetting to multiply by W₀. 12 g multiplies W₀ by 2 and by 3 instead of raising 2 to the power 3.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', growth rates: geometric growth
solution.final_answer: Option D: 16 g

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about gibberellins are correct?

(a) More than 100 gibberellins have been reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants.
(b) All gibberellins are basic in nature.
(c) GA₃ was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form.
(d) Gibberellins delay senescence, so fruits can be left on the tree longer to extend the market period.
(e) Gibberellins are derivatives of carotenoids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: More than 100 gibberellins (GA₁, GA₂, GA₃ ...) are known from fungi and higher plants; GA₃ was one of the first discovered and is the most intensively studied. All GAs are acidic. They are terpenes; it is ABA that is a carotenoid derivative. Gibberellins delay senescence, which extends the market period of fruits.
steps: (e) False: GAs are terpenes; ABA is the carotenoid derivative
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B and D include (b); option C includes (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', gibberellins
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethylene promotes vertical growth of seedlings and suppresses swelling of the axis.
Reason (R): Ethylene promotes senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially of leaves and flowers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Ethylene influences horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings, so the assertion reverses both effects. Ethylene does promote senescence and abscission of plant organs, especially leaves and flowers, so R is true.
steps: A: false, ethylene promotes horizontal growth and swelling of the axis
solution.why_others_wrong: A is the trap: it inverts the NCERT effects (horizontal growth, swelling of the axis).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', ethylene
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A grower wants a single compound that, applied as an aqueous spray, is readily absorbed and releases a growth regulator slowly inside the plant. It should hasten ripening of tomatoes and apples and accelerate abscission of flowers and fruits for thinning of cotton, cherry and walnut. The compound is:

solution.concept: Ethephon as a source of ethylene
solution.explanation: Ethephon is the most widely used compound as a source of ethylene. In aqueous solution it is readily absorbed and transported within the plant and releases ethylene slowly. Ethylene hastens fruit ripening (tomatoes, apples) and accelerates abscission of flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut).
steps: Effects described: ripening and abscission → ethylene
Compound that releases ethylene slowly in the plant → ethephon
solution.why_others_wrong: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used as a herbicide. Gibberellic acid delays senescence of fruits. Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor and does not release ethylene.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', ethylene
solution.final_answer: Option B: Ethephon

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed and each lobe is dithecous. How many microsporangia does such an anther have?

solution.explanation: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, each lobe having two theca (dithecous). The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure with four microsporangia at the corners, two in each lobe.
solution.why_others_wrong: Two counts only the lobes; one ignores both lobes and theca; eight doubles the real number.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option C: Four

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The prominent apertures in the exine of a pollen grain, where sporopollenin is absent, are called:

solution.explanation: The exine of the pollen grain has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent. The pollen tube comes out through one of the germ pores when the pollen germinates.
steps: Exine with apertures lacking sporopollenin → germ pores
solution.why_others_wrong: The micropyle is the opening of the ovule, the hilum is the junction of ovule and funicle, and lenticels are openings in the bark of woody stems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Germ pores

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Ovules generally differentiate a single megaspore mother cell (MMC). In which region of the nucellus is it differentiated?

solution.explanation: Ovules generally differentiate a single megaspore mother cell in the micropylar region of the nucellus. It is a large cell with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and it undergoes meiosis to form four megaspores.
steps: MMC → large cell, dense cytoplasm, prominent nucleus
Location → micropylar region of the nucellus
solution.why_others_wrong: The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule opposite the micropyle; the hilum and funicle lie outside the nucellus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', the pistil, megasporangium (ovule) and embryo sac: megasporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Micropylar region

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Among animals, the dominant biotic pollinating agents are:

solution.explanation: Bees, butterflies, flies, beetles, wasps, ants, moths, birds (sunbirds, hummingbirds) and bats are common pollinating agents, and some primates, arboreal rodents and reptiles also pollinate. Among the animals, insects, particularly bees, are the dominant biotic pollinating agents.
steps: Dominant biotic agents → insects, especially bees
solution.why_others_wrong: Birds, bats and rodents do pollinate some species, but none is the dominant group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Insects, particularly bees

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the embryo sac, the fusion of one male gamete with the two polar nuclei is called:

solution.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote. The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei in the central cell to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus; because three haploid nuclei are involved this is called triple fusion. The two fusions together make up double fertilisation.
steps: Male gamete + 2 polar nuclei → triple fusion
solution.why_others_wrong: Syngamy is fusion with the egg. Double fertilisation is the name for both fusions together. 'Generative fusion' is not a term NCERT uses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Triple fusion

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as:

solution.explanation: Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is called polyembryony. In many Citrus and mango varieties, nucellar cells develop into additional embryos.
steps: More than one embryo per seed → polyembryony
solution.why_others_wrong: Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilisation; apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation; polyploidy is an increase in whole chromosome sets.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony
solution.final_answer: Option C: Polyembryony

Statement I: In a transverse section, a typical microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers: the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the ovule) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Funicle
B. Hilum
C. Micropyle
D. Chalaza

List-II:

II. Stalk that attaches the ovule to the placenta

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about insect-pollinated flowers are correct?

(a) The majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar.
(b) When the flowers are small, a number of them are clustered into an inflorescence to make them conspicuous.
(c) Their pollen grains are generally light, non-sticky and produced in enormous numbers.
(d) Their pollen grains are generally sticky.
(e) In some species, the floral reward is a safe place for the pollinator to lay its eggs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Insect-pollinated flowers are mostly large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar; small flowers are clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous. Their pollen grains are generally sticky so they adhere to the pollinator's body. Rewards are nectar and pollen, and in some species a safe place to lay eggs (as in Amorphophallus and Yucca). Light, non-sticky pollen is a feature of wind-pollinated flowers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The majority of flowering plants produce unisexual flowers, so pollen rarely comes in contact with the stigma of the same flower.
Statement II: Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The majority of flowering plants produce hermaphrodite (bisexual) flowers, so pollen grains are likely to contact the stigma of the same flower. Continued self-pollination results in inbreeding depression, which is why flowering plants have evolved devices that discourage self-pollination.
steps: Statement I: false, most flowering plants have hermaphrodite flowers
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', outbreeding devices
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In most flowering plants, endosperm development precedes embryo development.
Reason (R): The zygote divides immediately after fertilisation, before the primary endosperm cell starts dividing.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to form the endosperm. Most zygotes divide only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed; this adaptation assures nutrition to the developing embryo. So A is true and R, which reverses the order, is false.
steps: R: false, most zygotes divide only after some endosperm has formed
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', post-fertilisation events: endosperm and embryo
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, apomixis (production of seeds without fertilisation) is seen in:

options.text: Some species of Asteraceae and grasses
All dioecious plants such as papaya

solution.explanation: Some flowering plants, such as some species of Asteraceae and grasses, have evolved a special mechanism, apomixis, to produce seeds without fertilisation. It is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
steps: NCERT examples → some Asteraceae and grasses
solution.why_others_wrong: Pea and groundnut form seeds after fertilisation. Dioecy is an outbreeding device. Banana forms fruits without fertilisation (parthenocarpy), and these fruits are seedless.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A microsporangium contains 40 microspore mother cells, and all of them complete microsporogenesis normally. Each resulting pollen grain eventually forms the usual number of male gametes. How many male gametes are formed in all?

solution.explanation: Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to form a tetrad of four microspores, each of which matures into a pollen grain. In each pollen grain the generative cell divides to form two male gametes.
solution.why_others_wrong: 160 counts pollen grains, not gametes. 80 assumes each mother cell gives two pollen grains. 640 assumes four gametes per pollen grain.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', microsporogenesis; pollen grain
solution.final_answer: Option C: 320

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Scutellum
B. Coleoptile
C. Hypocotyl
D. Plumule

List-II:
I. Hollow foliar structure enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia in a grass embryo
II. Cylindrical part of the embryonal axis below the cotyledons, ending in the radicle
III. Stem tip at the end of the epicotyl
IV. Single cotyledon of the grass family, situated towards one side of the embryonal axis

Hypocotyl → below cotyledons, ends in radicle (C-II)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about events in the embryo sac during and after fertilisation are correct?

(a) The primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm.
(b) The synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilisation.
(c) The zygote develops into the embryo.
(d) The pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of an antipodal cell.
(e) The two male gametes are formed by division of the vegetative cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The pollen tube enters one of the synergids (guided by the filiform apparatus) and releases two male gametes into its cytoplasm. These male gametes were formed by division of the generative cell. After double fertilisation, the primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm and the zygote into the embryo, while the synergids and antipodals degenerate.
steps: (d) False: the gametes are released into a synergid
(e) False: male gametes come from the generative cell
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', double fertilisation; post-fertilisation events
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Xenogamy is the only type of pollination that brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.
Reason (R): In xenogamy, pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of a different plant.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In autogamy pollen comes from the same flower, and in geitonogamy from another flower of the same plant; geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy because the pollen comes from the same plant. Only in xenogamy does pollen come from a different plant, so only xenogamy brings genetically different pollen to the stigma. R states that defining feature, so it explains A.
steps: R: true, pollen from a different plant
A different plant carries a different genotype → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: kinds of pollination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In plants that shed pollen in the three-celled condition, the pollen tubes carry the two male gametes from the beginning.
Statement II: In plants that shed pollen in the two-celled condition, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes before the pollen grain lands on the stigma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: After a compatible pollen lands, it germinates and its tube grows through the stigma and style. Where pollen is shed at the three-celled stage, the tube carries the two male gametes from the beginning. Where it is shed at the two-celled stage, the generative cell divides to form the two male gametes during the growth of the pollen tube in the stigma, i.e. after the pollen has landed.
steps: Statement II: false, the division happens during pollen tube growth in the stigma
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II shifts the timing of the generative cell division; that detail is the trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollen-pistil interaction
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a flowering plant with 2n = 24, how many chromosomes are present in a cell of the nucellus, the functional megaspore, an endosperm cell and a synergid, respectively?

solution.concept: Ploidy of ovule and embryo sac tissues
solution.explanation: The nucellus is sporophytic tissue of the parent plant (2n = 24). The megaspore is formed by meiosis (n = 12). The synergid is part of the female gametophyte formed from the megaspore by mitosis (n = 12). The endosperm comes from the primary endosperm nucleus formed by triple fusion (3n = 36).
solution.why_others_wrong: A treats the nucellus as haploid and the synergid as diploid. B forgets that the megaspore forms by meiosis. C treats the endosperm as diploid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', megasporogenesis; double fertilisation
solution.final_answer: Option D: 24, 12, 36 and 12

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Parthenocarpy can be induced through the application of growth hormones, and such fruits are seedless.
(b) Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction.
(c) In some species, the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilisation.
(d) Parthenocarpic fruits contain seeds formed by apomixis.
(e) Apomixis is the development of a fruit without fertilisation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation; it can be induced by growth hormones and the fruits are seedless. Apomixis is the production of seeds without fertilisation, an asexual process mimicking sexual reproduction; in some species a diploid egg forms without reduction division and develops into the embryo without fertilisation.
steps: (e) False: that describes parthenocarpy; apomixis produces seeds
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', apomixis and polyembryony; parthenocarpy
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In most water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering.
Reason (R): Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT facts about water pollination. The mucilaginous covering protects the pollen from getting wet in water. The rarity of water pollination (about 30 genera, mostly monocots) is a separate fact about its distribution and does not explain why the pollen has a protective covering.
steps: R is about how rare water pollination is, not about protecting pollen → B
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A is the trap: R is a true fact about the same topic but explains nothing about the mucilage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pollination: agents of pollination

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Gregor Mendel conducted his hybridisation experiments on garden peas over a period of:

solution.explanation: Mendel conducted hybridisation experiments on garden peas for seven years (1856–1863) and proposed the laws of inheritance in living organisms.
steps: Duration of Mendel's pea experiments → seven years, 1856 to 1863
solution.why_others_wrong: The other periods do not match NCERT; 1900 is the year his work was rediscovered.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In 1900, Mendel's results on the inheritance of characters were independently rediscovered by:

options.text: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak

solution.explanation: Mendel's work remained unrecognised for several decades. In 1900, three scientists, de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak, independently rediscovered his results on the inheritance of characters.
steps: 1900 → independent rediscovery by de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak
solution.why_others_wrong: Sutton and Boveri linked chromosome movement to Mendel's factors; Morgan and Sturtevant worked on linkage and gene mapping in Drosophila; Watson and Crick proposed the double helix of DNA.

solution.final_answer: Option A: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Henking (1891) traced a specific nuclear structure all through spermatogenesis in a few insects and named it the 'X body'. What did he observe about its distribution?

options.text: All the sperm received the X body
All the eggs lacked the X body
The X body was found only in somatic cells
Only 50 per cent of the sperm received the X body after spermatogenesis

solution.explanation: Henking observed that 50 per cent of the sperm received this structure after spermatogenesis while the other 50 per cent did not. He named it the X body but could not explain its significance; later it was named the X chromosome.
steps: Structure traced through spermatogenesis → X body
Distribution → only half the sperm received it
solution.why_others_wrong: Henking studied spermatogenesis and found the structure in only half the sperm, not all; he made no observation about eggs or restriction to somatic cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option D: Only 50 per cent of the sperm received the X body after spermatogenesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: α-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11.
Statement II: Thalassemia is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules, whereas sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Thalassemia is an autosome-linked recessive blood disease. α-thalassemia is controlled by two closely linked genes, HBA1 and HBA2, on chromosome 16; β-thalassemia is controlled by a single gene, HBB, on chromosome 11. Thalassemia is a quantitative problem (too few globin molecules) while sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem (incorrectly functioning globin).
steps: Statement I: false, it describes β-thalassemia; α-thalassemia: HBA1 and HBA2 on chromosome 16
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendelian disorders: thalassemia
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Failure of segregation of chromatids during the cell division cycle, resulting in the gain or loss of a chromosome, is called:

solution.explanation: Chromosomal disorders are caused by absence, excess or abnormal arrangement of chromosomes. Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division results in gain or loss of one or more chromosomes, called aneuploidy (as in Down's syndrome).
steps: Gain or loss of individual chromosome(s) → aneuploidy
solution.why_others_wrong: Polyploidy is an increase in a whole set of chromosomes; a point mutation changes a single base; crossing over exchanges segments between homologous chromosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: Aneuploidy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Multiple alleles can be found only when population studies are made.
Statement II: A single diploid individual can carry more than two alleles of the same gene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: When more than two alleles govern the same character, they are called multiple alleles (the ABO blood group gene I is the NCERT example). Since an individual has only two alleles of a gene, multiple alleles can be found only when population studies are made.
steps: Statement II: false, an individual has only two alleles of a gene
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', co-dominance and multiple alleles
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Failure of cytokinesis after the telophase stage of cell division increases the number of whole sets of chromosomes. This condition, called polyploidy, is often seen in:

solution.explanation: Failure of cytokinesis after telophase results in an increase in a whole set of chromosomes in an organism. This phenomenon is known as polyploidy, and this condition is often seen in plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: Polyploidy is not restricted to one human sex; bacteria are prokaryotes without such chromosome sets.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option B: Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In pea, a gene B controls starch synthesis. BB seeds are round with large starch grains, bb seeds are wrinkled with smaller starch grains, and Bb seeds are round with starch grains of intermediate size. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: B shows complete dominance for both seed shape and starch grain size
The alleles show co-dominance for seed shape
b is dominant for starch grain size and recessive for seed shape
B is dominant for seed shape, but for starch grain size the alleles show incomplete dominance

solution.concept: Dominance depends on the phenotype examined
solution.explanation: Heterozygous Bb seeds are round, so B appears dominant for seed shape. But Bb seeds have starch grains of intermediate size, so if starch grain size is taken as the phenotype, the alleles show incomplete dominance. Dominance is therefore not an autonomous feature of a gene; it depends on the phenotype chosen.
steps: Shape: Bb round like BB → B dominant
Starch grain size: Bb intermediate → incomplete dominance
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A ignores the intermediate grain size. Co-dominance would need both parental phenotypes to show in Bb. b is not dominant for either character.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', incomplete dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles
solution.final_answer: Option D: B is dominant for seed shape, but for starch grain size the alleles show incomplete dominance

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A pea plant of genotype RrYy is obtained by crossing RRYY with rryy. The two genes assort independently. The gametes produced by this F1 plant are:

options.text: Four kinds, RY, Ry, rY and ry, each with a frequency of 25 per cent
Two kinds, RY and ry, each with a frequency of 50 per cent
Four kinds, with RY and ry at 40 per cent each and Ry and rY at 10 per cent each

solution.explanation: Because the R/r and Y/y pairs segregate independently, each R or r gamete is equally likely to receive Y or y. The F1 therefore forms four kinds of gametes, RY, Ry, rY and ry, each with a frequency of 1/4. Random fusion of these gametes gives the 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 F2 ratio.
steps: R or r: 1/2 each; Y or y: 1/2 each
solution.why_others_wrong: Two kinds of gametes would mean complete linkage; unequal frequencies would mean linkage with recombination; nine is the number of F2 genotypes, not gamete types.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option A: Four kinds, RY, Ry, rY and ry, each with a frequency of 25 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In Mendel's monohybrid crosses, the recessive parental trait reappears in the F2 generation in a blended, intermediate form.
Reason (R): Alleles do not show any blending, and both parental characters are recovered as such in the F2 generation, though one of them is not seen in the F1.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the F1 the recessive trait is not expressed, but in the F2 it is expressed without any blending. The alleles do not blend; they segregate during gamete formation, so both parental characters are recovered as such in the F2. Hence A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false, the recessive trait reappears unblended
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: law of segregation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Morgan's dihybrid crosses in Drosophila, when the two genes were on the same chromosome, the parental gene combinations were much more frequent than the non-parental ones.
Statement II: Morgan used the term recombination to describe the generation of non-parental gene combinations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Morgan carried out several dihybrid crosses in Drosophila to study sex-linked genes. When the two genes were on the same chromosome, the proportion of parental gene combinations was much higher than that of the non-parental type. He attributed this to the physical association (linkage) of the genes and used the term recombination for the generation of non-parental gene combinations.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (disorder) with List-II (type).

List-I:
A. Haemophilia
B. Phenylketonuria
C. Down's syndrome
D. Turner's syndrome

List-II:
I. Trisomy of chromosome 21
II. Autosomal recessive Mendelian disorder
III. Absence of one X chromosome (45, X0)
IV. Sex-linked recessive Mendelian disorder

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disease. Phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Down's syndrome is caused by an additional copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy 21). Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one X chromosome (45 with X0).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about sex determination are correct?

(a) In the XO type of sex determination, all the eggs bear an additional X chromosome besides the autosomes.
(b) In Drosophila, the male has one X and one Y chromosome.
(c) In humans, the sex of the child is decided by the mother.
(d) Of the 23 pairs of chromosomes in humans, 22 pairs are autosomes, exactly the same in males and females.
(e) In birds, the male produces two different types of gametes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In XO type (as in grasshopper) all eggs carry an X besides the autosomes, while sperm are of two kinds. Drosophila and humans show XX-XY (male heterogamety). In humans 22 pairs are autosomes; the father produces X-bearing and Y-bearing sperm, so the sperm (father) decides the child's sex. In birds the female is ZW and produces two types of gametes, while the ZZ male produces one type.
steps: (e) False: in birds the female is heterogametic
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (c) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Polygenic traits usually show distinct alternate forms, such as tall and dwarf, with no intermediates.
Statement II: Polygenic traits are generally controlled by three or more genes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Mendel studied traits with distinct alternate forms. Polygenic traits, like human height and skin colour, instead show a gradient of phenotypes. Such traits are generally controlled by three or more genes, each allele making an additive contribution.
steps: Statement I: false, polygenic traits are spread across a gradient
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Red-green colour blindness occurs in about 8 per cent of males but only about 0.4 per cent of females.
Reason (R): The genes that lead to red-green colour blindness are located on the Y chromosome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Colour blindness occurs in about 8% of males and about 0.4% of females. This is because the genes that lead to red-green colour blindness are on the X chromosome: males have only one X, while a female is affected only if both her X chromosomes carry the gene. R puts the gene on the Y chromosome, which is false (a Y-linked trait would never appear in females).
steps: R: false, the genes are X-linked
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which feature of Mendel's experiments gave greater credibility to the data that he collected?

options.text: Use of Drosophila, which completes its life cycle in about two weeks
Study of traits that showed blending in the F1
Study of only one generation of offspring

solution.explanation: Mendel's experiments had a large sampling size, which gave greater credibility to his data. Confirmation over successive generations showed that his results pointed to general rules of inheritance. He was also the first to apply statistical analysis and mathematical logic to problems in biology.
steps: Large number of plants and crosses → greater credibility of data
solution.why_others_wrong: Drosophila was Morgan's material; Mendel chose traits with distinct alternate forms, not blending; he followed several generations.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option D: A large sampling size

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A man with blood group AB (IᴬIᴮ) marries a woman with blood group A who is heterozygous (Iᴬi). What fraction of their children are expected to have blood group A?

solution.concept: ABO blood groups: co-dominance and multiple alleles
solution.explanation: Gametes of the man: Iᴬ and Iᴮ; gametes of the woman: Iᴬ and i. The four equally likely children are IᴬIᴬ (A), Iᴬi (A), IᴬIᴮ (AB) and Iᴮi (B).
steps: Children: IᴬIᴬ, Iᴬi, IᴬIᴮ, Iᴮi (1/4 each)
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/4 counts only IᴬIᴬ. 3/4 wrongly counts IᴬIᴮ as group A, ignoring co-dominance. 1/3 treats the three phenotypes as equally likely.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', co-dominance and multiple alleles: ABO blood groups
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1/2

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A dihybrid AaBb, which received AB from one parent and ab from the other, is test-crossed with aabb. The 1000 progeny are: 440 AaBb, 430 aabb, 65 Aabb and 65 aaBb. The recombination frequency between the genes is:

solution.explanation: In a test cross, each progeny class shows the gamete received from the dihybrid parent. Parental gametes (AB, ab) give AaBb and aabb; non-parental (recombinant) gametes (Ab, aB) give Aabb and aaBb. Recombination frequency = recombinants / total. Sturtevant used such frequencies as a measure of the distance between genes.
solution.why_others_wrong: 87% is the parental fraction. 6.5% counts only one recombinant class. 26% doubles the recombinants.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option A: 13 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a plant, flower colour shows incomplete dominance (RR red, Rr pink, rr white), while height shows complete dominance (T, tall, over t, dwarf). The two genes assort independently. In the progeny of RrTt × RrTt, how many different phenotypes appear, and what fraction of the progeny is pink-flowered and tall?

solution.explanation: Treat each gene separately and multiply. Flower colour: Rr × Rr gives red : pink : white = 1 : 2 : 1, i.e. three phenotypes, pink = 1/2. Height: Tt × Tt gives tall : dwarf = 3 : 1, two phenotypes, tall = 3/4.
solution.shortcut: Number of phenotypes = product of phenotypes per gene: 3 × 2 = 6.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 and 9/16 assume complete dominance for both genes. 9 is the number of genotypes, not phenotypes. 1/4 uses 1/4 for pink (confusing it with red) instead of 1/2.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', incomplete dominance; inheritance of two genes
solution.final_answer: Option C: 6 phenotypes; 3/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Individuals heterozygous for sickle-cell anaemia (HbᴬHbˢ) appear apparently unaffected but are carriers of the disease.
Reason (R): The disease is controlled by a single pair of alleles, Hbᴬ and Hbˢ, and of the three possible genotypes only individuals homozygous for Hbˢ show the diseased phenotype.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Sickle-cell anaemia as an autosomal recessive trait
solution.explanation: Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait. Only HbˢHbˢ individuals show the disease. Heterozygotes therefore appear apparently unaffected, yet they carry Hbˢ and have a 50% probability of passing it to each child, i.e. they are carriers. R gives the recessive nature of the allele, which is the reason for A.
steps: Only the homozygote is affected → heterozygote unaffected carrier → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendelian disorders: sickle-cell anaemia
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the chromosomal theory of inheritance and Morgan's work are correct?

(a) One reason Mendel's work remained unrecognised was that the use of mathematics to explain biological phenomena was new and unacceptable to many biologists of the time.
(b) Chromosomes occur singly in diploid cells, whereas genes occur in pairs.
(c) The two alleles of a gene pair are located on homologous sites on homologous chromosomes.
(d) Drosophila is suitable for genetic studies because it can be grown on a simple synthetic medium, completes its life cycle in about two weeks and a single mating gives a large number of progeny.
(e) Morgan found that genes located on the X chromosome always assort independently of each other.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mendel's work went unrecognised partly because communication was not easy and the use of mathematics in biology was new and unacceptable. Chromosomes as well as genes occur in pairs, and the two alleles of a gene pair lie on homologous sites of homologous chromosomes. Morgan chose Drosophila for its simple culture, two-week life cycle, large progeny and clear sex differences. He found that genes on the X chromosome did not assort independently: they were linked.
steps: (b) False: both chromosomes and genes occur in pairs
(e) False: linked X-chromosome genes did not segregate independently
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (b) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', chromosomal theory of inheritance; linkage and recombination
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In pleiotropy, a single phenotype is controlled by several genes acting together.
Statement II: In co-dominance, the F1 generation resembles both parents.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Pleiotropy is the reverse of Statement I: a single gene exhibits multiple phenotypic expressions, usually because the gene affects metabolic pathways that contribute to different phenotypes. A single phenotype controlled by several genes describes polygenic inheritance. In co-dominance the F1 resembles both parents (as in blood group AB), unlike incomplete dominance where it is intermediate.
steps: Statement I: false, it describes polygenic inheritance
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I swaps the definitions of pleiotropy and polygenic inheritance; that swap is the trap.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', pleiotropy; co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A colour-blind woman marries a man with normal colour vision. Which outcome is expected among their children?

options.text: All daughters colour blind; all sons normal
All sons colour blind; all daughters with normal vision but carriers
Half the sons and half the daughters colour blind

solution.explanation: The woman is XᶜXᶜ, so every child receives an Xᶜ from her. Sons receive their only X from the mother and Y from the father, so all sons are XᶜY (colour blind). Daughters receive the father's normal X as well, so all are XᶜX (normal vision, carriers).

Father X Y → daughters get X, sons get Y
Sons XᶜY: colour blind; daughters XᶜX: carriers with normal vision

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex-linked inheritance: colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option C: All sons colour blind; all daughters with normal vision but carriers

questions.question_text: In a nucleoside, the nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of the 1' carbon of the pentose sugar through a:

solution.explanation: A nitrogenous base is linked to the 1'C OH of the pentose sugar through an N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside. A phosphate group linked to the 5'-OH of the nucleoside through a phosphoester linkage gives a nucleotide, and nucleotides are joined through 3'-5' phosphodiester linkages to form a polynucleotide.
solution.why_others_wrong: Phosphoester and phosphodiester bonds involve the phosphate; hydrogen bonds join complementary bases of the two strands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Histones are positively charged proteins because they are rich in the basic amino acid residues:

solution.explanation: In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is packaged with a set of positively charged basic proteins called histones. Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine, which carry positive charges in their side chains.
solution.why_others_wrong: Glutamic and aspartic acids are acidic; glycine, alanine, cysteine and methionine are not basic residues.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Griffith's experiments with Streptococcus pneumoniae, the S strain bacteria formed smooth, shiny colonies because they have:

options.text: Pili all over the cell surface

solution.explanation: Griffith grew Streptococcus pneumoniae on culture plates. Some strains produced smooth, shiny colonies (S); others produced rough colonies (R). This is because the S strain bacteria have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat, while the R strain does not. Mice infected with the S strain die of pneumonia.
steps: Smooth colonies → S strain → mucous (polysaccharide) coat
R strain → no coat, rough colonies
solution.why_others_wrong: The difference between S and R strains is the polysaccharide coat; a protein capsid belongs to viruses.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by three regions. These are:

options.text: An operator, the structural gene and a repressor
An origin, a promoter and an operator
A promoter, the structural gene and a terminator
A cap, the structural gene and a poly-A tail

solution.explanation: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by three regions: a promoter, the structural gene and a terminator. questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): George Gamow suggested that the genetic code should be made up of three nucleotides.
Reason (R): With four bases, a triplet code gives 4³ = 64 combinations, enough to code for all 20 amino acids, whereas a doublet code would give only 4² = 16.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why the code is a triplet
solution.explanation: Gamow, a physicist, argued that since there are only four bases and they must code for 20 amino acids, the code must use a combination of bases. A doublet gives only 16 combinations, fewer than 20; a triplet gives 64, more than enough. R is the reasoning behind A.
steps: R gives the reason for a triplet code → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the lac operon of E. coli, the inducer that switches on the operon is:

solution.explanation: Lactose is the substrate for β-galactosidase and it regulates switching on and off of the operon; hence it is termed the inducer. In its presence the repressor is inactivated by interaction with the inducer, so RNA polymerase can transcribe the operon.
steps: Substrate that inactivates the repressor → inducer → lactose
solution.why_others_wrong: Glucose is not the lac inducer; the repressor (from the i gene) is what the inducer inactivates; β-galactosidase is the z gene product that hydrolyses lactose.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option D: Lactose

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A double-stranded DNA molecule has 5 × 10⁶ base pairs. Taking the distance between two consecutive base pairs as 0.34 nm, what is the length of this DNA molecule?

solution.concept: Length of DNA from base pairs
solution.explanation: Length = number of base pairs × distance between consecutive base pairs. The two strands run side by side, so the length depends on the number of base pairs, not on the number of nucleotides.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.85 mm divides by 2, as if the two strands shared the length; 3.4 mm multiplies by 2, as if the nucleotides of both strands were laid end to end; 17 mm is a power-of-ten slip in converting nm to mm.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain: double helix
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1.7 mm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When the phosphate moiety at the 5'-end of the sugar is free in a polynucleotide chain, that end is referred to as the 5'-end of the chain.
Statement II: The backbone of a polynucleotide chain is formed by the nitrogenous bases, while the sugar and phosphate project outward from it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A polynucleotide has a free phosphate at the 5'-end of the sugar (5'-end) and a free 3'-OH at the other end (3'-end). The backbone is formed by sugar and phosphates; the nitrogenous bases linked to the sugar project from the backbone.
steps: Statement II: false, the sugar-phosphate chain is the backbone and bases project from it
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, packaging of chromatin at a higher level requires an additional set of proteins called non-histone chromosomal (NHC) proteins.
Reason (R): In prokaryotes such as E. coli, the negatively charged DNA is held with some positively charged proteins in a region termed the nucleoid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In eukaryotes, DNA is wrapped around histone octamers to form nucleosomes, which form chromatin fibres; higher-level packaging needs non-histone chromosomal proteins. Prokaryotes lack a defined nucleus; their DNA is held with some positively charged proteins in the nucleoid. R is a true statement about prokaryotes and says nothing about why eukaryotic chromatin needs NHC proteins.
steps: R describes prokaryotic DNA, unrelated to eukaryotic higher-order packaging → B
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (scientist) with List-II (contribution).

A. Har Gobind Khorana

C. Severo Ochoa

List-II:
I. Chemical method for synthesising RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases
II. Proposed the central dogma of molecular biology
III. Enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) that polymerises RNA with defined sequences without a template
IV. Cell-free system for protein synthesis that helped decipher the code

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Khorana's chemical method synthesised RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases (homopolymers and copolymers). Nirenberg's cell-free system for protein synthesis finally helped decipher the code. Ochoa's enzyme, polynucleotide phosphorylase, polymerised RNA with defined sequences in a template-independent manner. Crick proposed the central dogma (DNA → RNA → protein).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about DNA replication are correct?

(a) Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates serve both as substrates and as a source of energy for polymerisation.
(b) In long DNA molecules, replication occurs within a small opening of the DNA helix called the replication fork.
(c) Replication can start at any random point in the DNA.
(d) In eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place in the S-phase of the cell cycle.
(e) A failure of cell division after DNA replication results in aneuploidy.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: dNTPs serve as substrates and provide energy. Because the two strands cannot be separated along their entire length (it needs too much energy), replication occurs within a small opening, the replication fork. Replication starts only at a definite region, the origin of replication. In eukaryotes it occurs in the S-phase, and a failure of cell division after DNA replication results in polyploidy.
steps: (c) False: replication begins at the origin of replication
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (c) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In eukaryotes, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA), the precursor of mRNA, is transcribed by:

solution.explanation: In the eukaryotic nucleus there are three RNA polymerases besides the one in organelles. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S); RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs; RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, hnRNA.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pol I makes the larger rRNAs; Pol III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs; DNA polymerase replicates DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option D: RNA polymerase II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, the structural genes are split: the coding sequences (exons) are interrupted by introns.
Reason (R): Introns are the sequences that appear in the mature, processed RNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Eukaryotic structural genes are split genes. Exons are the coding (expressed) sequences that appear in mature or processed RNA; introns (intervening sequences) do not appear in mature RNA because they are removed by splicing. So A is true and R, which says the opposite about introns, is false.
steps: R: false, exons appear in mature RNA; introns are spliced out
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription unit and the gene; transcription in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are features of the genetic code?

(a) The codon is a triplet; 61 codons code for amino acids and 3 codons do not code for any amino acid.
(b) Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon; hence the code is degenerate.
(c) The codon is read in mRNA in a contiguous fashion; there are no punctuations.
(d) The code is absolutely universal, with no exceptions in any organism or organelle.
(e) The three codons that do not code for amino acids are recognised by specific tRNAs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The code is a triplet: 61 codons code for amino acids and 3 are stop codons. It is degenerate (some amino acids have more than one codon) and is read contiguously without punctuation. It is nearly universal: UUU codes for phenylalanine from bacteria to humans, but there are exceptions in mitochondrial codons and in some protozoans. There are no tRNAs for stop codons.
steps: (e) False: there are no tRNAs for stop codons
solution.why_others_wrong: Options B, C and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code; translation
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The lac operon of E. coli consists of one regulatory gene and three structural genes. The enzyme transacetylase is coded by:

solution.explanation: The lac operon has a regulatory gene i, which codes for the repressor, and three structural genes: z codes for β-galactosidase (hydrolyses lactose into galactose and glucose), y codes for permease (increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides) and a codes for transacetylase.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty treated the purified extract of heat-killed S-strain bacteria with different enzymes before mixing it with live R-strain bacteria. Which treatment inhibited transformation?

options.text: Digestion with both proteases and RNases

solution.concept: Biochemical nature of the transforming principle
solution.explanation: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA) from heat-killed S cells. Protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was neither protein nor RNA. Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, showing that DNA caused the transformation.
steps: DNase → transformation inhibited → DNA is the transforming principle
solution.why_others_wrong: Proteases and RNases, alone or together, left the DNA intact, so transformation still took place.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: biochemical characterisation of transforming principle

The project was closely associated with the rapid development of bioinformatics. The sequence of chromosome 1 was completed only in May 2006, the last of the 24 human chromosomes. Repeated sequences make up a very large portion of the genome.
steps: (d) False: chromosome 1 was the last to be completed (May 2006)
(e) False: repeated sequences form a very large portion
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e). (d) is the trap: chromosome 1 has the most genes, but it was the last to be sequenced.

questions.subject: Botany

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A very low level of expression of the lac operon has to be present in the cell all the time.
Reason (R): Permease, a product of the lac operon, increases the permeability of the cell to β-galactosides; without it, lactose cannot enter the cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Basal expression of the lac operon
solution.explanation: Lactose must enter the cell before it can act as an inducer. Its entry depends on permease (y gene product), which is itself made by the lac operon. So a very low level of expression has to be present all the time; otherwise lactose could never get in to induce the operon. R gives this reason.
steps: No permease → no lactose entry → no induction; so basal expression is needed → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: RNA world and the choice of DNA
solution.explanation: RNA was the first genetic material and acted as both genetic material and catalyst. Being a catalyst it was reactive and unstable, so DNA evolved from RNA with chemical modifications that make it more stable. DNA, being more stable, is preferred for storage of genetic information; RNA is better for its transmission.
steps: Statement II: false, DNA is more stable and is preferred for storage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Within the coding region of a gene, the three base pairs that make up one complete codon are deleted. What is the most likely effect on the encoded protein?

options.text: One amino acid is deleted, and the reading frame remains unaltered from that point onwards
The reading frame shifts, so every codon after the deletion is read differently
Translation cannot begin because the initiator codon is lost
The protein becomes three amino acids shorter

solution.explanation: The code is read in triplets without punctuation. Insertion or deletion of one or two bases shifts the reading frame (frameshift). Insertion or deletion of three bases, or a multiple of three, inserts or deletes one or more codons, and hence one or more amino acids, and the reading frame remains unaltered from that point onwards.
steps: Deleting three bases → one codon, hence one amino acid, fewer
Frame after the deletion is unchanged
solution.why_others_wrong: A frameshift needs deletion of one or two bases (not a multiple of three). The deletion is within the gene, not at the start codon. Three bases make one codon, so only one amino acid is lost, not three.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', mutations and genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option A: One amino acid is deleted, and the reading frame remains unaltered from that point onwards

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about translation are correct?

(a) For initiation, the ribosome binds to the mRNA at the start codon (AUG), which is recognised only by the initiator tRNA.
(b) During elongation, complexes of an amino acid linked to tRNA sequentially bind to the appropriate codons in mRNA.
(c) At the end, a release factor binds to the stop codon, terminating translation and releasing the complete polypeptide.
(d) There are two sites in the large subunit of the ribosome where subsequent amino acids bind, close enough to form a peptide bond.
(e) There are specific tRNAs for each of the stop codons.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Translation starts when the ribosome binds the mRNA at AUG, recognised only by the initiator tRNA. In elongation, aminoacyl-tRNA complexes bind in sequence by base pairing of anticodon and codon; the large subunit has two sites where successive amino acids bind close enough to form a peptide bond. At the end, a release factor binds to the stop codon. There are no tRNAs for stop codons.
steps: (e) False: there are no tRNAs for stop codons
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (e); option D also leaves out true statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', tRNA the adapter molecule; translation

Statement I: Primary treatment of sewage involves physical removal of particles, large and small, through filtration and sedimentation.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: To compare the productivity of different ecosystems, primary productivity is expressed in units of:

Units: g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the reasons for conserving biodiversity are correct?

(a) Under the narrowly utilitarian argument, humans derive countless direct economic benefits from nature, such as food, firewood, fibre and construction material.
(b) More than 25 per cent of the drugs currently sold in the market worldwide are derived from plants.
(c) Bioprospecting means exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance.
(d) The ethical argument holds that every species has an intrinsic value, even if it is not of current economic value to us.
(e) Pollination of plants by bees, birds and bats is the standard example of the narrowly utilitarian argument.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The narrowly utilitarian argument rests on direct economic benefits: food, firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products and medicines (more than 25% of drugs sold worldwide come from plants). Bioprospecting explores biodiversity for products of economic importance. The broadly utilitarian argument covers ecosystem services such as oxygen production and pollination by bees, bumblebees, birds and bats. The ethical argument says every species has intrinsic value.
steps: (e) False: pollination is a broadly utilitarian benefit
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D include (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: why should we conserve biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.question_text: Illustrating the latitudinal gradient in diversity, NCERT notes that Colombia, located near the equator, has nearly:

solution.explanation: Species diversity generally decreases from the equator towards the poles. Colombia, near the equator, has nearly 1,400 species of birds, while New York at 41° N has 105 species and Greenland at 71° N only 56 species. India, with much of its land in the tropics, has more than 1,200 species of birds.
solution.why_others_wrong: 105, 56 and 1,200 are NCERT's figures for New York, Greenland and India respectively.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: latitudinal gradients

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: In situ and ex situ conservation
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about biodiversity conservation are correct?

(a) Many nations find it economically not feasible to conserve all their biological wealth, because the number of species waiting to be saved from extinction far exceeds the conservation resources available.
(b) The 'Earth Summit' held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits.
(c) The World Summit on Sustainable Development was held in 2002 in Rio de Janeiro.
(d) At the World Summit on Sustainable Development, 190 countries pledged to achieve, by 2010, a significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss.
(e) National parks are a means of ex situ conservation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Faced with the conflict between development and conservation, many nations find it unrealistic and economically not feasible to conserve all their biological wealth: the number of species waiting to be saved from extinction invariably far exceeds the conservation resources available. National parks are protected areas, a means of in situ conservation. The Earth Summit (Rio de Janeiro, 1992) called on nations to conserve biodiversity and use it sustainably. Its follow-up, the World Summit on Sustainable Development, was held in 2002 in Johannesburg, South Africa, where 190 countries pledged a significant reduction in the rate of biodiversity loss by 2010.
steps: (c) False: the 2002 summit was in Johannesburg
(e) False: national parks are in situ
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (c) or (e). (c) is the trap: it swaps the venue of the 2002 summit with that of the 1992 summit.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a coevolved plant-pollinator mutualism, the extinction of one partner invariably leads to the extinction of the other.
Reason (R): When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it in an obligatory way also become extinct.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Co-extinction is one of the four major causes of biodiversity loss: when a species becomes extinct, species associated with it obligatorily also become extinct. A coevolved plant-pollinator pair depends on each other obligatorily, so the extinction of one invariably leads to the extinction of the other. R is the general principle of which A is an instance.
steps: Obligatory partners die out together → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity: causes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

Yet to be discovered: > 1,00,000 plants and > 3,00,000 animals
